title: Unawareness of continuous sensor data sharing
description: The user (wearer) continuously shares sensitive telemetry (heart rate, steps, GPS, timestamps) by wearing the device without necessarily realizing the full privacy implications or extent of collection.
assumptions: User has not been explicitly informed or has not read privacy policy details.

title: Disclosure of sensitive personal telemetry in transit
description: Sensor data including GPS position and health metrics flows from user to device, exposing potentially identifiable and sensitive information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted or processed locally but still represents disclosure to the device.
uncertainty_note: Context suggests all types possible for EE->Process; this is a core disclosure risk for health/location data.

title: Identifiability via wearable telemetry
description: The wearable device (P1) receives and can process data that directly identifies or re-identifies the individual wearer through unique patterns in heart rate, steps, and especially GPS.
assumptions: Device stores or uses the data in a way that links back to the user.

title: Explicit disclosure of personal sensor data across device boundary
description: The wearable device intentionally transfers exercise sessions, GPS traces, device ID and timestamps to the companion app. Per the minimality principle this volume of location and activity data may exceed what is strictly required for basic sync, creating an avoidable explicit data disclosure.

title: Identifiability of user via device ID combined with GPS traces
description: On receipt the companion app can link the persistent device identifier with precise location traces and timestamps, enabling re-identification of the data subject even if other identifiers are absent.

title: Linkability of multiple exercise sessions through shared device ID
description: The wearable (source) emits a stable device identifier with every batch, allowing any observer of the flow to link successive sessions to the same individual.

title: Unawareness as a user sharing personal health data
description: The user (wearer) manually logs sensitive personal information including calorie intake, meals, and weight entries into the companion app. This act of sharing may occur without full awareness of how the data will be processed, stored, shared with third parties, or used for profiling by the app and connected systems.
assumptions: The flow involves direct user input of health-related personal data to the process.
uncertainty_note: Directly supported by retrieved context [5] for U.1.2; applies to this ExternalEntity->Process interaction per mapping table [4].

title: Health data disclosure via storage
description: The health log store receives and persists sensitive personal health data (calorie intake, weight, exercise) from the app, creating an explicit disclosure boundary where data could be accessed or leaked if access controls or encryption are insufficient.
assumptions: The datastore is part of the system boundary and stores data long-term.

title: User unawareness of health log persistence
description: The companion app shares detailed health logs without ensuring the user is fully aware of or has consented to the storage and potential processing in the health log store.
assumptions: No explicit consent or notice mechanism is described in the flow.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify UI or consent flows; this is inferred from typical app behavior.

title: Identifiability through health metadata in transit
description: The data flow carries health logs that inherently identify or can be linked to the individual user, increasing identifiability risk during transmission to the store.
assumptions: Logs are associated with a user account or device ID.

title: Explicit disclosure of precise GPS traces
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) writes detailed GPS location traces with timestamps to the Location History Store, transferring personal movement data across the process-datastore boundary. This may violate the minimality principle if more data is stored than strictly necessary for the intended functionality.
assumptions: The location history feature is designed to store full traces, but the explicit collection and storage could be avoidable or reduced in granularity.

title: Linkability of location points over time
description: The Location History Store receives and retains timestamped GPS traces, enabling long-term linking of location data points to reconstruct the user's movements and potentially identify patterns or routines.
assumptions: Data is stored persistently without anonymization or aggregation that would prevent linking.
uncertainty_note: Context does not explicitly cover linkability for Process->DataStore but mapping table indicates L is applicable at D.

title: Explicit disclosure of sensitive health data
description: Health Log Store shares calorie, weight, and exercise logs (personal data) with Analytics Service for health-condition analysis; violates minimality if more data transferred than strictly necessary.
assumptions: Data is personal and identifiable health information.
uncertainty_note: Context [5] on Dd applies approximately; explicit by design but potentially avoidable over-sharing.

title: Linkability of logs across sessions
description: Analytics service links calorie/weight/exercise data across multiple sessions to enable detailed health-condition profiling and potential re-identification.

title: Disclosure of location history enabling routine inference
description: The flow transfers detailed location history from the store to the analytics service, allowing derivation of daily routines and movement patterns. This constitutes an explicit data disclosure of sensitive personal data that may exceed minimality requirements if not strictly necessary for the health analytics purpose.
assumptions: The location data includes timestamps and positions across multiple sessions, making patterns derivable.

title: User unawareness of location pattern analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service processes the received location history to derive routines without ensuring user awareness or consent for this specific secondary use of their data.
assumptions: Users may have consented to location storage but not to cross-session analytics for movement patterns.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify consent mechanisms; this is inferred from typical health app scenarios.

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health data return flow
description: The Health Analytics Service shares inferred health insights (risk indicators, summaries, trend flags) back to the app without evidence of integrated privacy-cybersecurity risk management, potentially violating regulations for sensitive health data processing and transmission.
uncertainty_note: Context provides Nc.3 but applicability to this specific return flow is inferred from health data sensitivity rather than directly stated.

title: Unintended disclosure of sensitive health inferences via dashboard
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) displays trends and inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals on the user dashboard; without adequate screen privacy controls or session timeouts this can lead to disclosure of highly sensitive personal health data to bystanders or unauthorized viewers.
assumptions: Assumes the mobile app dashboard can be viewed by others in proximity (e.g. shoulder-surfing or shared device use).

title: User unawareness of inference implications
description: The user (EE1) receives inferred condition indicators without clear explanation of how the data was derived, potential accuracy limitations, or downstream privacy consequences of acting on or sharing those signals.
assumptions: Based on typical health-inference app behavior where explanations may be limited.

title: Non-compliance with health-data regulations
description: Displaying inferred medical risk signals (eating disorder, diabetes) constitutes processing of special-category health data; failure to implement required safeguards, consent mechanisms or transparency under GDPR/HIPAA equivalents creates compliance risk.
assumptions: Inferred from the sensitive nature of the displayed indicators and context on Nc linking to legal risk.

title: Explicit data disclosure of full health dataset to third-party
description: The Health Analytics Service shares the full health and location dataset with the Cloud Hosting Provider for hosting and replication, constituting an explicit transfer of personal data to a third party.
assumptions: The dataset contains personal data as implied by 'health and location dataset'.

title: Receipt and storage of sensitive personal data by external cloud
description: The Cloud Hosting Provider receives and stores/replicates the complete health and location dataset, enabling potential further disclosure or access by the third party.
assumptions: Third-party provider may not have equivalent privacy protections or may access the data.
uncertainty_note: Depends on contractual and technical controls not specified in flow.

title: Linkability via metadata of data transfer to cloud
description: The data flow itself may allow linking the analytics service's data sharing activities with specific health datasets being hosted externally.
assumptions: Flow metadata or volume could reveal patterns.
uncertainty_note: Context does not strongly support this; may be weak evidence.
